text:
mike_l: CloudWatch alert at 03:12 UTC — analytics-db export spike. Metric S3ExportOps jumped x15. Found repeated COPY/UNLOAD operations to s3://redwood-exports/exports/ by service account 'etl-service@prod'.
Sample query snippet we pulled from query log:
```
COPY (SELECT id, email, phone, created_at FROM users WHERE last_login < '2022-01-01') TO 's3://redwood-exports/exports/16823.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv);
```
Link to log snapshot: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/home#logsV2:log-groups (redacted)
Is this scheduled backfill gone rogue or unauthorized access?

ana_sec: Oncall security here — checking audit trails. Seeing ~42 export objects created in last 2h, most include email/phone columns. Escalating to P1 (possible exfil).

kevin_infra: Temporary containment: disabled new STS sessions for role svc-etl-prod and put a deny s3:PutObject inline policy on that role. Commands run: `aws sts revoke-session --role arn:aws:iam::123456:role/svc-etl-prod` (short) and `aws iam put-role-policy --role-name svc-etl-prod --policy-name deny-put-prod`

julia_data: That role is used by nightly-backfill. We merged backfill v2 last night — quick look shows the window filter was incorrectly removed in the SQL (bad diff). Rolling back the backfill deploy to v1.4.2 now.

audit-bot: Audit entries: user=etl-service role=svc-etl-prod source_ip=54.239.12.3 action=CopyToS3 resource=redwood-exports/exports/16823.csv kms=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abc status=Success count=42

ana_sec: Confirming KMS usage — exported objects show SSE-KMS with customer-managed key arn:.../key/abc. Need to verify key policy for overly permissive principals. Also request: snapshot DB and preserve S3 objects for forensics. Marking evidence-preservation checklist.

kevin_infra: S3 objects currently SSE-KMS. I've added a temporary bucket policy to deny GetObject unless via our VPC endpoint and created object lock/retention for the exported prefix. Command (summary): `aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-exports --policy file://deny-get-unless-vpc.json` and `aws s3api put-object-lock-configuration ...`

mike_l: Notifying legal/compliance now. @compliance — need guidance on PII thresholds and customer notification requirements.

compliance: Received. Provide estimated affected rows and sample object keys (redacted) and we'll advise on notification timelines and regulators. Also check contractual obligations for data handling.

security-bot: Incident created: INC-20260320-17. Response lead assigned: ana_sec. Postmortem template: https://internal/redwood/incidents/templates/data-exfil-postmortem

julia_data: Preliminary root cause: regression in backfill job removed the time-window clause -> full-table selection executed repeatedly by the job. No signs of credential compromise; actions tied to service role sessions and known deploy artifact. Patch: re-add time-window filter, add LIMIT guard, and redeploy.

ana_sec: Actions completed so far: 1) rotated DB read-only user credentials used by ETL; 2) revoked existing sts sessions for svc-etl-prod; 3) preserved CloudTrail, DB query logs, and S3 object metadata; 4) flagged objects for forensics download (read-only). Next: forensic team to verify whether objects were downloaded externally.

kevin_infra: Follow-ups: schedule KMS key policy review to ensure only pipeline roles can use the key and require encryption context checks for export operations. Also adding an alert: export-count per role > 5/hr -> fire PagerDuty.

mike_l: Short-term RBAC proposal: disallow svc-etl-prod s3:PutObject on production bucket except when assumed by pipeline-aggregator role. That will limit blast radius for service account bugs. Can infra apply as emergency change?

julia_data: I'll update the CI checks for backfill jobs: 1) a preflight that verifies a time-window or row cap is present for any export, 2) tests that assert only allowed columns (no PII) are exportable. Will submit PR today.

ana_sec: Drafting internal comms and incident summary. If forensic confirms external downloads, we'll prepare customer notifications. Tagging @cto for awareness.

mike_l: Good work — keep this thread for all updates. Please add short notes when each action completes. :thumbsup:
